WRITTEN OFFER FOR CORRESPONDING SOURCE CODE (FFmpeg, LGPL-2.1-or-later)
=======================================================================

This container image includes a build of FFmpeg that is dynamically linked
and licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or (at
your option) any later version ("LGPL-2.1-or-later"). The full text of the
LGPL-2.1 is reproduced in this image's THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

The bundled FFmpeg is configured with "--disable-gpl --disable-nonfree", so
the shared libraries (libavutil, libavcodec, libavformat, libswscale,
libswresample, libavfilter, libavdevice) are LGPL-2.1-or-later. FFmpeg is
linked against:
  - nv-codec-headers (MIT) for NVENC/CUVID hardware acceleration,
  - SVT-AV1 (BSD-3-Clause-Clear + Alliance for Open Media Patent License 1.0)
    for royalty-free CPU AV1 encoding,
  - dav1d (BSD-2-Clause) for royalty-free software AV1 decoding, and
  - libvpx (BSD-3-Clause) for royalty-free CPU VP9 encoding.

In accordance with LGPL-2.1 section 6, we make the following offer.

1. Complete corresponding source
--------------------------------
The exact upstream sources used to build the bundled libraries are the release
archives listed below. We apply no patches to FFmpeg, SVT-AV1, or dav1d; for
libvpx we apply exactly one upstream commit on top of the release tag, noted
with that entry. The "modifications" relevant to the LGPL are therefore limited
to the build configuration, which is fully specified by the build script
referenced in section 2.

  - FFmpeg 9.0.1
    Source:   https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-9.0.1.tar.xz
    SHA-256:  cf38e0e28c7e5605942c4a77755349b0145804a397af37eb1fb4c77cb237f635

  - SVT-AV1 v4.2.0
    Source:   https://gitlab.com/AOMediaCodec/SVT-AV1 (tag v4.2.0)
    Commit:   9292ec8e32bce26f781f277ec8739b53426c4300

  - dav1d 1.5.4
    Source:   https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d (tag 1.5.4)
    Commit:   54706fc6bc0cdecab7e9593974a4039cc038fca7

  - libvpx v1.16.0
    Source:   https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx (tag v1.16.0)
    Commit:   1024874c5919305883187e2953de8fcb4c3d7fa6
    Patch:    commit d5f35ac8d93cba7f7a3f7ddb8f9dc8bd28f785e1 from the same
              repository, applied on top of the tag. It is the upstream fix for
              CVE-2026-2447 (a heap buffer overflow in the VP9 encoder), which
              no libvpx release tag contains yet.

  - nv-codec-headers n13.0.19.1
    Source:   https://github.com/FFmpeg/nv-codec-headers (tag n13.0.19.1)
    Commit:   88fee5c37318c991a8762d423530f91681e32e3a

2. Build configuration and scripts
----------------------------------
The complete, self-contained script that downloads the above sources, pins
and verifies their integrity, configures FFmpeg (including the exact
"./configure" flags), builds the libraries, and packages them is published
publicly at:

  https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-evaluator/blob/main/third_party/ffmpeg/tar.sh

Running that script reproduces the FFmpeg build shipped in this image. It
documents the full configuration required to relink the application against a
modified version of the FFmpeg libraries, as contemplated by LGPL-2.1.

3. Relinking
------------
The FFmpeg libraries are used as dynamically loaded shared objects
(".so" files) placed on the loader path (usr/local/lib). You may replace them
with your own build of the corresponding FFmpeg source, subject to the FFmpeg
libraries' exported ABI, and the packaged "ffmpeg"/"ffprobe" binaries and the
application will use your libraries instead.

4. How to obtain the source
----------------------------
The sources in section 1 are available at the URLs listed there. In addition,
for a period of at least three (3) years from the date you received this
product, and valid for as long as we offer spare parts or customer support for
this product, we will provide, to anyone who possesses this offer, a complete
machine-readable copy of the corresponding source for the bundled
LGPL-covered FFmpeg libraries (and the build configuration in section 2) for a
charge no more than our cost of physically performing source distribution.

To request the source, contact NVIDIA and reference "Cosmos Evaluator FFmpeg
LGPL corresponding source" together with the FFmpeg version above:

  https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-evaluator/issues

This offer is valid to anyone in receipt of this information.
